artworks.title: Battle of the Ships (Ambrosian Iliad)
artworks.description: Milan, Biblioteca Ambrosiana Cod. F. 205 Inf.: late antique miniature of the fight at the hulls — Hector's push to the Achaean ships as Homer's crisis of Books XIII–XVI.

artworks.title: The Siege of the Greek Camp (Ambrosian Iliad)
artworks.description: Ambrosian Iliad: Trojans pressing the Greek camp and ships — the wall broken, the fleet at stake before Patroclus enters the fight.

artworks.title: Ajax Defending the Greek Ships against the Trojans
artworks.description: Flaxman's outline for Church's Story of the Iliad: Telamonian Ajax alone at the prow while Hector calls for fire — the ship-fight distilled to a single stubborn defence.

artworks.title: Polydamas Advising Hector to Retire from the Trench
artworks.description: Flaxman: Polydamas urges caution at the trench before Hector presses on to the ships — the omen ignored on the road to the fleet.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Petersen's beach assault and Greek camp under fire borrow the Iliad's ship-fight stakes — Hector at the hulls as Hollywood spectacle.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Books XIII–XVI: Poseidon rouses the Achaeans, Hector breaks the wall, and fire touches the first ship — the crisis that forces Patroclus into arms.

popCulture.title: Ajax the Great
popCulture.description: Telamonian Ajax holding the ship against Hector remains the Iliad's image of stubborn defence at the waterline.

popCulture.title: Hector
popCulture.description: The Trojan who reaches the ships and calls for fire — the battle for the fleet is Hector's high-water mark before Patroclus turns the tide.
